analysis: The experiment succeeded: host validation macro-average HR@10 reached 0.5800, exceeding the stated previous best of 0.535 by 0.045. Category HR@10 was 0.620 for Movies_and_TV, 0.645 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.465 for Electronics, and 0.590 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics remains the weakest category. These results support further investigation of masked-item reconstruction, but do not isolate bidirectional attention or auxiliary masking as the cause of the improvement. No test performance is available.
code_summary: Trained one independent bidirectional transformer per category, with 96-dimensional shared item embeddings, learned position embeddings, two transformer blocks, two attention heads, and dropout 0.2. Length-64 training prefixes always mask the final target and randomly mask 20% of historical positions. Training uses sampled softmax with 256 shared uniform negatives, equally weighting final-target and auxiliary reconstruction losses, optimized by AdamW. Validation selects a single checkpoint per category by HR@10 with NDCG as a tie-breaker. Prediction appends a mask to the history and scores candidates using the final hidden state, tied item embeddings, and a jointly learned item bias. Dataset routing loads exactly one trained checkpoint per category; no ensemble or separately fitted scores are used.
